title: Business Phrasal Verbs
completion_message: ¡Fantástico! Dominar los Phrasal Verbs es el secreto para sonar natural y fluido en ambientes corporativos.

parts.visual:
Reuniones y Proyectos: 
- Set up (Organizar / Configurar). Ej: Let's set up a meeting. 
- Put off (Posponer). Ej: We have to put off the meeting until Friday. 
- Call off (Cancelar). Ej: The boss called off the project.
parts.audio: Meetings and projects. Set up means to organize or arrange. For example: Let's set up a meeting. Put off means to postpone. For example: We have to put off the meeting until Friday. Call off means to cancel. For example: The boss called off the project.

parts.visual:
Ideas y Propuestas: 
- Bring up (Mencionar / Sacar un tema). Ej: Don't bring up the budget. 
- Turn down (Rechazar). Ej: They turned down our offer. 
- Figure out (Descubrir / Resolver). Ej: We need to figure out a solution.
parts.audio: Ideas and proposals. Bring up means to mention a topic. For example: Don't bring up the budget. Turn down means to reject an offer. For example: They turned down our offer. Figure out means to find a solution or understand something.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el Phrasal Verb correcto para la situación de negocios.

questions.question: I need to ____ up a meeting with the client for next week. (Organizar).
The CEO is sick, so we have to ____ off the meeting until tomorrow. (Posponer).
The strike is terrible. We must ____ off the event completely. (Cancelar).
We offered them $10,000, but they ____ it down. (Rechazaron).
questions.explanation: Turn down = rechazar una oferta o solicitud.

questions.question: During the meeting, Sarah ____ up the issue of the budget. (Mencionó / Sacó a relucir).
questions.explanation: Bring up (pasado: brought up) = mencionar o introducir un tema.

questions.question: We have a problem with the server, and we need to ____ it out. (Resolverlo / Entenderlo).
questions.explanation: Figure out = encontrar una solución, resolver, entender algo.

questions.question: Our company is going to ____ over a smaller competitor. (Adquirir / Tomar el control).
questions.explanation: Take over = tomar el control o adquirir una empresa.

questions.question: Please ____ out this form with your personal details. (Rellenar).
questions.explanation: Fill out (o fill in) = rellenar un formulario.

questions.question: Sales have gone ____ by 20% this year! (Subido).
Unfortunately, our profits have gone ____. (Bajado).
I will ____ into the problem and report back tomorrow. (Investigar).
We need to ____ out the new software before buying it. (Probar).
questions.explanation: Test out / Try out = probar para ver si funciona.

questions.question: The IT department is going to ____ down the servers for maintenance. (Apagar).
Can you ____ up with a better idea? (Proponer / Idear).
questions.explanation: Come up with (an idea) = idear, proponer algo nuevo.

questions.question: The negotiations fell ____ at the last minute. (Fracasaron).
questions.explanation: Fall through = fracasar, no llegar a un acuerdo.

questions.question: Please ____ on. I'm listening. (Continúa).
Could you ____ over the report one more time to check for errors? (Revisar).
We need to ____ ahead with the plan despite the risks. (Seguir adelante).
I can't ____ out what the problem is. (Descubrir / Entender).
They ____ off the meeting because nobody could attend. (Cancelaron).
